extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, members of mathematical societies, and the general public interested in the European Mathematical Society
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the European Mathematical Society's aims, governance, committees, publications, Congress and prize eligibility/criteria. Includes procedural details (council, statutes) and award-specific requirements (age limits, purpose, and selection intent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote mathematical research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society aims to 'Promote mathematical research, both pure and applied.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMS seeks to serve mathematicians in universities, research institutes and other higher education forms by promoting research activity across pure and applied mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist and advise on mathematical education
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society aims to 'Assist and advise on problems of mathematical education.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMS' remit includes advising on education issues affecting mathematicians and mathematical training in higher education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address broader relations of mathematics to society
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society aims to 'Concern itself with the broader relations of mathematics to society.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMS considers the societal role and impact of mathematics as part of its mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster international interaction between mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society aims to 'Foster interaction between mathematicians of different countries.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMS promotes cross-border collaboration and communication among European (and international) mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a European mathematical identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society aims to 'Establish a sense of identity amongst European mathematicians.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of EMS' goal is community-building and representing a shared European mathematical identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent the mathematical community in supra-national institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society aims to 'Represent the mathematical community in supra-national institutions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMS acts as an organizational representative (e.g., affiliate/associate member statuses with IMU and ICIAM) in international bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council composition and governance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The governing body (the council) comprises delegates representing member societies and delegates for institutional and individual members; it meets every two years and appoints the president and executive committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMS rules are set down in statutes and bylaws; the council and executive committee are responsible for running the society and appointing officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing committees and their remit
rubrics_metrics.description: EMS maintains standing committees such as Applications and Interdisciplinary Relations, Developing Countries, Mathematical Education, ERCOM, Ethics, European Solidarity, Meetings, Publications and Electronic Dissemination, Raising Public Awareness of Mathematics, Women in Mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These committees handle specialized areas of EMS activity and policy (e.g., publications, meetings, ethics, outreach, education).

rubrics_metrics.name: European Congress of Mathematics (ECM) frequency and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Congress of Mathematics is held every four years at different locations around Europe and is organised by the EMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ECM is the main EMS congress where key society activities (including awarding EMS Prizes) occur; events may be postponed for exceptional circumstances (e.g., ECM 2020 postponed to 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: EMS Prizes eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten EMS Prizes are awarded at the ECM 'to recognize excellent contributions in Mathematics by young researchers not older than 35 years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prizes are awarded every four years at the ECM and target early-career researchers (explicit age cap provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Felix Klein Prize eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Felix Klein Prize is awarded to 'a young scientist or a small group of young scientists (normally under the age of 38) for using sophisticated methods to give an outstanding solution, which meets with the complete satisfaction of industry, to a concrete and difficult industrial problem.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endowed by the Institute for Industrial Mathematics in Kaiserslautern; emphasizes industrial applicability, sophistication of methods, and satisfactory concrete solutions to difficult industrial problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Otto Neugebauer Prize eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Otto Neugebauer Prize is awarded to a researcher or group 'for highly original and influential work in the field of history of mathematics that enhances our understanding of either the development of mathematics or a particular mathematical subject in any period and in any geographical region.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endowed by Springer Verlag; recognizes originality and influence in history of mathematics scholarship and its contribution to understanding mathematical development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simon Norton Prize eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Simon Norton Prize for Mathematics Outreach is awarded to individuals, teams or partnerships 'whose work in any area of mathematics engagement has had an outstanding and demonstrable impact or influence on its audience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced in 2024; emphasizes demonstrable outreach impact and influence on audiences across mathematics engagement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize age-limits and award timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Several EMS awards specify age limits (e.g., EMS Prizes: not older than 35; Felix Klein Prize: normally under 38) and are tied to ECM or other periodic schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is explicitly age-based for some awards and award schedules are linked to EMS-organized events (notably ECM every four years).

rubrics_metrics.name: EMS Press publishing scope and format
rubrics_metrics.description: EMS is the sole shareholder of EMS Press which publishes over 25 academic journals and has published over 200 books since 2003 in both print and digital formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMS Press publishes journals, books and since 2021 the EMS Magazine; publications include open access offerings and a wide disciplinary range (journal list provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: EMS Magazine publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Magazine of the European Mathematical Society (EMS Magazine) is quarterly and open access, featuring news and expositions of recent developments in mathematical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formerly the Newsletter of the European Mathematical Society; details include ISSN/eISSN and named editor-in-chief; intended as outreach and exposition for the mathematical community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship of reference works
rubrics_metrics.description: EMS sponsors the Encyclopedia of Mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsorship indicates EMS supports major reference resources in mathematics as part of its publication and outreach activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutes and bylaws as governing legal framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The EMS's rules are set down in its statutes and bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutes and bylaws provide the formal legal/procedural standards governing membership, governance, committees, and society operations.
